question: What did Apple's fiscal 2025 annual report disclose about the Digital Markets Act?
answer: Apple's fiscal 2025 annual report disclosed that on March 25, 2024, the European Commission opened a formal noncompliance investigation against Apple under Article 5(4) of the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA), relating to how developers may communicate and promote offers to end users for apps distributed through the App Store and how developers may conclude contracts with those end users. On June 24, 2024, the Commission announced it had opened an additional formal investigation regarding whether Apple’s new contractual requirements for third-party app developers and app marketplaces may violate the DMA (the "Article 6(4) Investigation"). On April 23, 2025, the Commission fined Apple €500 million in the Article 5(4) Investigation and issued a cease and desist order requiring Apple to remove technical and commercial restrictions that prevent developers from steering users to alternative distribution channels outside the App Store. Apple has appealed the Commission’s Article 5(4) decision. Also on April 23, 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings in the Article 6(4) Investigation. If the Commission makes a final determination in the Article 6(4) Investigation that there has been a violation, it can issue a cease and desist order and may impose fines up to 10% of Apple’s annual worldwide net sales. The Commission may also seek to impose additional fines if it deems that Apple has violated a cease and desist order. Apple believes it complies with the DMA and has continued to make changes to its compliance plan in response to feedback and engagement with the Commission. [1]
